Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117154/assets/599b5392add89a6a22eb6c2232fedbdd26704ebf849bb05d7de52a6d81dcfb6a.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{x}{2}-z},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117154/assets/9e7c6fad45d9d85bad5ca16a2000e4d44a1739ab70797e41ae94945a4ffb02ef.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{x}{2}-z}
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-x/2-z}dy\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}[y]_{y=0}^{y=3-x/2-z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(3-\frac{x}{2}-z)-0\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}3-\frac{x}{2}-z\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(3-\frac{x}{2})z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((3-\frac{x}{2})(2)-\frac{{2}^{2}}{2})-0\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}4-x\,dx \\  & ={[4x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(8-2)-0 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
